![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

When constructing storage keys or identifiers from multiple fields, return null if any of the required fields are missing or nullish, rather than interpolating empty or partial values. Ensure that any lookups or operations using that key fail closed with an explicit error rather than constructing or using a malformed key.

```javascript
const blockerKey = (!normalizedBlocker.blockerId || !normalizedBlocker.blockerScope)
  ? null
  : normalizedBlocker.blockerId + "|" + normalizedBlocker.blockerScope;
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. When constructing storage keys or identifiers from multiple fields, return null if any of the required fields are missing or nullish, rather than interpolating empty or partial values.
</details>

Fixed in 14dcda466. `readBlockers` now derives `blockerKey` only from the raw required fields, leaves malformed blocker keys as `null`, preserves malformed records independently, and fails display closed with `malformed_blocker_present`. Added regression coverage for missing blockerId and missing blockerScope staying separate.

Fixed in 14dcda466. `rightsStatusReasonCode` now emits no reason only for allowed statuses and falls back to `rights_display_blocked` for unknown unallowed statuses such as `rights_pending`. Added regression coverage for that fail-closed diagnostic.
